title: QUIC RFC 9000 Preferred Address Migration Source Protection Work Item
summary: Add focused requirement-home proof and trace ownership for the remaining S9P6P3 preferred-address migration-source protection tail.
planned_changes:
- Add direct positive proof that a client-side new-address migration validates and promotes the same address-family preferred server address for IPv4 and IPv6 cases.
- Add direct positive proof that preferred-address traffic from a changed source remains candidate-path protected and anti-amplification-limited.
- Add direct positive proof that a probe packet from a different address initiates client-address validation with a PATH_CHALLENGE before promotion.
- Link the S9P6P3-0006, S9P6P3-0009, and S9P6P3-0010 requirements to dedicated architecture, work-item, and verification artifacts.
- Regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage and run focused verification.
verification_plan: Run the focused S9P6P3-0006/0009/0010 requirement-home filter, run a Release build, run the full Release no-build solution test suite, regenerate QUIC requirement coverage triage, validate SpecTrace JSON, and check the diff for whitespace errors.
out_of_scope: Multipath scheduling or multiple active outbound paths.
Changing path-validation, anti-amplification, or peer connection-ID runtime behavior outside the focused proof.
completion_notes: Completed as focused proof over the existing preferred-address candidate-path validation, anti-amplification, and promotion behavior.
